name: France
note: A doctor or nurse attests the death on an electronic certificate (CertDc) whose administrative part goes straight to the commune and whose cause-of-death part goes to Inserm. A relative or other informed person declares the death to the officier de l'état civil, or the hospital or care home notifies within 24 hours, and the acte de décès is drawn up. The commune sends INSEE a bulletin within a week; INSEE updates the RNIPP, strikes the person from the electoral register and notifies authorised users such as social protection bodies. Banks and life insurers must check RNIPP deaths every year, and the death file is published monthly as open data.

steps.title: Health professional states and attests the death
steps.who: A physician (practising or retired), a third-cycle medical student or authorised foreign-trained practitioner, or a volunteer registered nurse (infirmier diplômé d'Etat).
steps.summary: The professional who finds the death completes the certificat de décès; no coffin may be closed without it. The administrative part goes to the commune of death.

steps.title: Electronic death certificate (CertDc), administrative part sent to the commune and funeral operator
steps.who: The health professional who attested the death.

deadline.text: dans les meilleurs délais; transmitted sans délais

steps.summary: The certificate is drawn up electronically by default and the administrative part is sent by secure electronic channel to the commune of death (with a téléservice for communes), the funeral operator and, if the body is moved, the commune of deposit. Paper is allowed only outside hospitals/EHPAD or if the service is down.

steps.title: Medical cause of death sent to Inserm (CépiDc)
steps.who: The certifying health professional; Inserm manages the cause-of-death database.
steps.summary: The medical part, which carries no name or NIR, is encrypted and sent to Inserm, which keeps the national cause-of-death base used by Santé publique France, regional health agencies and the SNDS.

steps.title: Violent or suspicious death referred to police and prosecutor
steps.who: The certifying professional indicates a 'problème médico-légal'; a police officer assisted by a doctor draws up a procès-verbal; cremation then needs the parquet's authorisation.
steps.trigger: Signs of violent death or other suspicious circumstances.
steps.summary: Burial cannot proceed until police, with a doctor, record the state of the body; the coffin-closure permit requires a certificate stating there is no medico-legal problem, and cremation in such cases needs the prosecutor's leave.

steps.title: Police transmit the particulars to the registrar
steps.who: The officier de police who drew up the procès-verbal.
steps.summary: In police cases the acte de décès is drawn up from the information in the police report.

steps.title: Declare the death to the officier de l'état civil
steps.who: A relative of the deceased, or anyone holding the most exact and complete information on the deceased's civil status.
steps.summary: The officier de l'état civil of the commune where the death occurred draws up the acte de décès on the declaration. The Code civil sets no general deadline (the commonly stated 24 hours could not be verified from statute); institutions have 24 hours (next step).

steps.title: Hospital, care home or prison notifies the registrar
steps.who: Directors of health establishments and of social/medico-social establishments for the elderly; prison wardens.
steps.summary: Establishments must notify the officier de l'état civil within 24 hours and keep a register of declarations.

steps.title: Registrar informs the prosecutor of a found body
steps.who: Officier de l'état civil of the presumed place of death; procureur de la République.
steps.summary: An acte de décès is drawn up whenever a body is found and can be identified; the prosecutor is told so identity can be established.

steps.title: Mayor authorises coffin closure, burial or cremation
steps.localName: autorisation de fermeture du cercueil / d'inhumation / de crémation
steps.who: The maire of the place of death (closure, cremation) or of the place of burial (inhumation), on presentation of the certificat de décès.
steps.trigger: Request by the funeral operator or family.
steps.summary: Closure of the coffin, burial and cremation each need a mayoral authorisation, which rests on the medical certificate rather than on the acte de décès; burial and cremation permits may be sent electronically.

steps.title: Copy of the acte sent to the commune of last domicile; mention on the birth record
steps.who: The officier de l'état civil who drew up the acte.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death outside the commune of domicile.
steps.summary: The acte is transcribed in the domicile commune's registers, and the death is noted in the margin of the birth record.

steps.title: Full copies of the acte de décès available to anyone
steps.localName: copie intégrale de l'acte de décès
steps.who: Any person may obtain a full copy; the prosecutor may restrict it where the circumstances endanger people named in the acte.
steps.summary: Unlike birth and marriage records, death records are open: full copies can be issued to anyone.

steps.title: Commune sends the death bulletin to INSEE (RNIPP)
steps.who: Officier de l'état civil of the commune of death; INSEE as keeper of the RNIPP.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the administrative part / drawing up of the acte.

deadline.text: une semaine à compter de l'établissement de l'acte

steps.summary: On receiving the certificate the commune sends INSEE a bulletin (name, birth date, sex, domicile, date and place of death, acte number); the décret sets one week for deaths. The RNIPP records date and place of death.

steps.title: RNIPP notifies civil-status changes to authorised users (social protection bodies)
steps.who: INSEE notifies authorised users of the répertoire, which include basic social security schemes, benefit bodies and supplementary health and pension bodies.
steps.summary: INSEE notifies each authorised user of changes to a person's civil status under a user-specific identifier. The décret does not name the death notification separately; the operational feed (SNGI) is not in the text read.

steps.title: Tax administration uses the RNIPP to certify identities
steps.who: DGFiP and customs services as authorised users of the NIR/RNIPP.
steps.summary: The DGFiP is an authorised RNIPP user for certifying identities in tax files; whether it receives a systematic death feed is not stated in the text read.

steps.title: INSEE strikes deceased electors from the répertoire électoral unique
steps.who: INSEE, which keeps the REU, and informs the mayors concerned.
steps.summary: INSEE removes deceased electors from the single electoral register directly and passes the change to the communes.

steps.title: Heirs file the succession declaration with the tax administration
steps.who: Heirs, donees and legatees (usually through the notary).

deadline.text: six mois à compter du jour du décès (death in metropolitan France)

steps.summary: The déclaration de succession is due within six months of a death in metropolitan France, one year otherwise.

steps.title: Notary queries FICOBA and FICOVIE for the deceased's accounts and life policies
steps.who: The notary settling the estate (and heirs, for FICOBA); insurers must report life contracts to the tax administration.
steps.summary: The notary obtains from the tax administration the list of the deceased's bank accounts (FICOBA) and life-insurance/capitalisation contracts (FICOVIE).

steps.title: Life insurers must check the RNIPP at least yearly (loi Eckert)
steps.who: Life insurers, institutions de prévoyance and unions, through the authorised professional bodies (AGIRA).
steps.summary: Insurers must find out at least once a year whether each insured person has died, using RNIPP death data obtained through the professional bodies.

steps.title: Beneficiary asks AGIRA whether the deceased named them in a life policy
steps.who: Any natural or legal person, proving the death, via the authorised professional body; insurers must reply within one month.

deadline.text: transmitted within 15 days; insurer answers within one month

steps.summary: The professional body forwards the request to all life insurers within 15 days; an insurer that finds the requester named as beneficiary has one month to tell them.

steps.title: Banks must check the RNIPP yearly for deceased account holders
steps.localName: comptes inactifs; fichier des personnes décédées
steps.who: Credit, e-money and payment institutions, directly or via a mandated person, under an INSEE convention.
steps.summary: Banks must consult RNIPP death data every year to identify deceased holders; they may obtain the fichier des personnes décédées extracted from the RNIPP.

steps.title: INSEE publishes the monthly fichier des personnes décédées as open data
steps.who: INSEE via data.gouv.fr; anyone may download it.
steps.summary: Every death recorded in the RNIPP is published once, uncorrected, in the following month's open-data file (name, birth and death details, acte number).

registrationDeadlineDays.note: 24 hours is statutory for hospitals, care homes and prisons (Code civil art. 80, 84). The Code civil sets no deadline for a family declaring a death at home; the 24-hour rule stated in official guidance could not be read (service-public.fr refused).

informantDuty.note: A relative or anyone with the best knowledge of the deceased's civil status declares; institutions' directors must notify within 24 hours; police transmit in violent deaths.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of certificates; a death posing a 'problème médico-légal' goes to police and the parquet instead.

electronicRegistration.note: The death certificate is electronic by default (CertDc) and reaches the commune electronically; the declaration itself and the acte are not described as electronic.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques (RNIPP), kept by INSEE

governmentPropagation.note: Commune → INSEE bulletin within a week; INSEE updates the RNIPP, notifies authorised users (social protection bodies) and strikes the elector from the REU.

certificateAccess.note: Full copies of death records may be issued to anyone, subject to a prosecutor's restriction for safety reasons.

privateSectorVerification.note: Life insurers (loi Eckert) and banks must consult RNIPP death data yearly; the death file is also open data.

gaps: No statutory general deadline for a family's déclaration de décès found in the Code civil (arts. 78–87); the 24-hour figure appears only in official guidance on service-public.fr, which the egress proxy refused (www.service-public.fr and service-public.fr).

insee.fr and www.insee.fr refused by the egress proxy, so INSEE's own pages on the RNIPP, SNGI and the 'fichier des personnes décédées' could not be read; the data.gouv.fr dataset page was used instead.

The operational feed from the RNIPP to social security (SNGI managed by CNAV) and to CPAM/health insurance is not described in the texts read; the step relies on décret 82-103 art. 9 (notification of civil-status changes to authorised users) and décret 2019-341 art. 2.
Whether the DGFiP receives a systematic death feed (rather than using the RNIPP to certify identities) is unverified.
Passports/identity cards and driving licences (ANTS): no statutory death notification route found.
No legal requirement of a public death notice or notice to creditors; nothing recorded for the 'public' stage.

Code civil art. 81–82 (police procès-verbal) and the parquet route; the Code de procédure pénale art. 74 (death of unknown cause) could not be retrieved by number through the Legifrance API search and is not cited.
